habitat: Open plains; grasslands; deserts; steppes; savannah; and low hills
story: In the diverse world of birds, the Steppe Eagle (Aquila nipalensis) stands out. This species, part of the Accipitridae family, is a resident of Open plains; grasslands; deserts; steppes; savannah; and low hills. Its IUCN Red List status is Endangered (EN), which serves as a call to action for habitat preservation. The Steppe Eagle is more than just a bird; it is a symbol of the rich biodiversity that we must protect. Through this poster, we hope to foster a greater understanding and appreciation for the Steppe Eagle and its role in the ecosystem.
Every poster is crafted to inspire curiosity about our planet's incredible biodiversity.
